fit: Clinical chart association with fall status
assessment: Table 2 shows hallucination history in 53.3% of Parkinson fallers and 37.5% of nonfallers. Methods mention visual hallucinations. The study's outcome is falls and fractures and the exposure comparison does not measure dried figs.

fit: Postmortem tissue comparison with one recorded visual history
assessment: The study compared complex I in brain samples from 10 Parkinson and 12 control donors. The clinical table records visual hallucinations in one donor with seizures. It does not systematically measure visual recurrence or culinary fig exposure.

fit: Neuropharmacology review with cited visual symptom and medication reports
assessment: The review discusses visual modality, vivid dreams and drug response evidence. It cites overlapping hallucination and illusion categories and distinct uncontrolled treatment trials. These are cited observations and no dried-fig comparison.

fit: Alzheimer autopsy and symptom history by pathology group
assessment: Hallucinations are documented in 10/24 with amygdala Lewy bodies and 9/30 without, using item-specific chart denominators and undifferentiated modality. The study gives no significant contrast or fig exposure.

The review names visual hallucinations as a symptom of Lewy body dementia and describes diagnostic imaging patterns. No new visual comparison is measured. Figures are scan illustrations and the review does not assess figs.

fit: Separate conference member observations in alternate clinical contexts
assessment: The case reports on pages 243, 252 and 279 describe biochemical disturbance with visual symptoms, diagnosis revised to progressive supranuclear palsy, and visual impairment with Charles Bonnet syndrome, respectively. Figures are illustrations. No member supplies a dried-fig contrast for Parkinson visual frequency.

fit: Primary outpatient sleep and hallucination/illusion overlap
assessment: Altered dreams overlapped with the combined hallucination or illusion category. Sleep fragmentation was not associated directly with this category in the model. A combined category is not a separate visual event rate.

fit: Uncontrolled quetiapine follow-up in Parkinson disease
assessment: The open-label cohort of 35 had improved psychiatric measures over 12 months. Dopaminergic regimens changed in many participants. The abstract distinguishes hallucinations and delusions without a separately reported visual episode rate.
In the 12-person Parkinson study the authors describe improvement in hallucinations and sleep disturbance. The abstract lacks a comparator, visual item count and fig exposure.

fit: Open tacrine or donepezil cognition and motor comparison
assessment: The 11-person study uses cognitive and motor scales. A reported change in cognition is a separate endpoint from a visual symptom. Distinct from the rivastigmine cohort.
